description: We are a team of four aspiring developers passionate about technology, innovation and space exploration. We enjoy solving problems, sharing ideas and learning through practical experiences. We aim to bring creativity, teamwork and dedication to the NASA Space Apps Challenge while developing an innovative and meaningful project.
summary:
ASTRA: Mission Control is an interactive astronaut training game that puts players in charge of a simulated lunar outpost. Players explore the base, complete mission activities, and manage oxygen, water, food, power, and habitat condition. Their choices affect the outpost, while rover surveys and sample collection introduce basic ideas about planetary exploration.

ASTRA addresses the challenge of making space missions and their resource trade-offs easier to understand through hands-on play. Its campaign takes players from the Moon toward Mars and Europa, turning complex mission concepts into an accessible experience. NASA science and space mission information helped shape the learning content, while the outpost, resource values, and events are clearly presented as fictional simulations. ASTRA matters because it can spark curiosity about space exploration and help young learners see how planning and teamwork support missions beyond Earth.
details:
ASTRA: Mission Control is an interactive astronaut training game where players explore a simulated lunar outpost and help keep its crew safe. Players monitor oxygen, water, food, power, and habitat condition, complete mission activities, and use a rover to collect a virtual sample. As they progress, they prepare for missions to Mars and Europa.

The project makes space exploration easier to understand by letting players experience the choices and resource challenges astronauts may face. NASA science and space mission information inform the game’s learning content, while the outpost and its resource rules are fictional simulations. ASTRA is important because it turns space science into an engaging, hands-on experience that can spark curiosity, teach problem-solving, and inspire young people to imagine future missions beyond Earth.
